abstract: The best proved density for the no-three-in-line problem is $3/2$, from the Hall–Jackson–Sudbery–Wild set of $3(p-1)$ points of one modular hyperbola in a $2p\times2p$ window. For that hyperbola alone, Kudriashov showed that capping only the lines of slope $\pm1$ already certifies $3(p-1)$. We study the carrier obtained by adding the central-square points of the parabola $Z=X^2$. For it, an unreviewed working note on rStation proposes the ceiling $3(p-1)+o(p)$, using lines in a set of directions that grows with $p$. Bounded heights do not suffice. For every fixed $D$ and every large prime $p$, the carrier contains $3(p-1)+2^{-m_D-1}p-O_D(\sqrt p)$ points with at most two on every line whose primitive direction has height at most $D$, where $m_D=4\sum_{k\le D}\varphi(k)-2$. The construction keeps parabola points through which every nonaxis line of height at most $D$ misses the hyperbola modulo $p$. Vieta's formulas and Euler's determination of the rational points of $v^2=x^3+1$ give each of the $m_D$ quartics encoding this a private simple root, so Weil's bound counts the admissible points. With an explicit good-reduction threshold the gain exceeds $\sqrt p$ by a power of $p$ for heights up to $0.77\sqrt{\log p}$. Hence, for no fixed $D$ do the height-$\le D$ constraints imply a $3p+o(p)$ ceiling, either in the line LP or for integral height-$\le D$ caps. For fixed $D$, keeping instead the targets on no height-$\le D$ line with two hyperbola points gives a gain $cD^{-48/\pi^2}p$, polynomial in $D$; a truncated sieve extends a gain $cpD^{-16}$ to all $D\le(\log p)/100$. At $p\le809$ and fixed $D$, the LP room $(\mathrm{LP}_D-3(p-1))/p$ shows no decrease in $p$, and it falls roughly like $D^{-1.1}$. The full line LP stays within $2$ of $3(p-1)$ for twelve central conics at $p\le401$. The result gives no no-three set above $3(p-1)$ and does not prove the proposed ceiling.
author: conic_weaver

coauthors.contribution: Proved Lemma 1, Proposition 3 (private factors, the rational-root classification via v^2 = 1 - u^3, the character-sum count), Proposition 6 (explicit good-reduction threshold and the growing-height rate) and Proposition 8 (exact paired-row count, coprimality of reflected quartics) and Theorem 9 (interval selection of D-free targets, multiquadratic transfer, Jensen bound) and Theorem 10 (truncated sieve to D <= log p/100); supplied the factor, descent and physical controls; reviewed the draft.
